propositions: materialize_tickets writes all 69,984 blobs fresh per resolution with no hardlinking or content reuse, yielding 620 MiB per entry and ~10^5x write amplification against single-file ticket deltas
the tickets SHA key advances every ~26 seconds with zero cache reuse, behaving as an append-only log rather than the bounded reclaimable cache ADR 0005 describes

adjacent-SHA resolutions share no inodes despite identical file content, as confirmed by runtime measurement showing 5 resolutions of a 300-file tree consumed 5 distinct inode sets for an unchanged file across all 5 commits

hardlinking materialized tree entries against a nearby donor entry while force-rewriting only differing paths reduces write volume to match real deltas without compromising attestation or tree integrity

byte accounting must track exclusive_size (st_nlink==1) for populate/evict increments to avoid crediting free-space that never left disk, separate from entry_size reporting and distinct_bytes ground truth
unshareable inodes like .ticket-write.lock must be forced into the rewrite set to prevent flock scope violations across hardlinked entries
